frequency_question: How often do central banks deploy incremental reserve ratios within a specific 4-month window when systemic liquidity surplus reaches elevated thresholds?
membership_rule: Includes any formal secondary reserve ratio or incremental cash reserve ratio mandate by a major central bank; excludes standard permanent reserve ratio adjustments.

cases.name: PBOC Reserve Requirement Ratio (RRR) targeted cuts/hikes (various 2010-2024)
Central Bank of Brazil Compulso adjustments (2011-2012)
Bank of Russia temporary reserve requirement adjustments (2022)

provenance_note: claims 25 cases from only 4 named (6.2x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 4 named historical instances of targeted incremental reserve ratio tools deployed globally out of roughly 25 comparable systemic liquidity surplus cycles.
known_gaps: Vrying definitions of liquidity instruments across different jurisdictions.
skeleton: Central bank policy cycles since 2000 involving liquidity management tools: approximately 4 major episodes of unexpected incremental reserve requirements applied to manage sudden liquidity surges across major emerging markets.
multiplier: 4 episodes across 25 years yielding an annualized base rate of approximately 16% for any given 4-month period under similar liquidity precursor states.
validity_reason: Central bank monetary policy frameworks and liquidity management toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year horizons.
